name: Dirty Negroni

cookwares.name: coffee filter or fine-mesh strainer if fat-washing

instructions.primary_message: Fill a mixing glass with gin, sweet vermouth, Campari, and olive brine.
Add ice and stir until thoroughly chilled, about 20 seconds.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with 1 to 3 olives of your choice on a cocktail pick and serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: negroni, dirty negroni, olive negroni, savory cocktails, negroni variation

description: A dirty Negroni adds a splash of olive brine to the classic Negroni formula. It combines gin, Campari, sweet vermouth, and olive brine for a savory, bitter, and balanced twist.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 large (preferably clear) ice cube for serving; Castelvetrano, Manzanilla, or Picholine olives, for garnish

Notes: For a richer, silkier variation, prepare a fat-washed batch ahead of time: In a resealable container (such as a 680 g Mason jar), combine 120 ml gin, 120 ml sweet vermouth, 120 ml Campari, and 60 ml olive brine with 120 ml extra-virgin olive oil and about 12 Castelvetrano olives. Seal and freeze for at least 24 hours. Once the olive oil has solidified into a cap, scoop it off and strain the remaining liquid through a coffee filter or fine-mesh strainer. Store the strained cocktail base in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. To serve, pour 90 ml of the fat-washed cocktail base straight into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with 1 to 3 olives and serve immediately.
author: Kelli Solomon
